summary: Move the John the Baptist title to III Part act.
rationale: Maʕmiḏono/Maʕməḏono names the person baptizing, not an action or a baptism recipient. Existing 59/16,32,42 quotation is retained once with its references.

data.turoyo: mərre d oṯət maʕməḏinalux b əšme d Mšiḥo, gəd d uxlət gdowət xdoṯayna ḥalal hat ste.
data.translation: Sie sagten: Wenn du kommst und wir dich im Namen des Messias taufen, dann wirst du essen und auch du wirst rein wie wir.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell; 1pl agent and 2sg patient suffix, with baptismal naming formula.

data.turoyo: amma d oṯət w d maʕmaḏnolux, maʕməḏinalux b əšme d Mšiḥo, tox axul aʕmayna.
data.translation: Aber wenn du kommst und ich dich taufe, wir dich taufen, im Namen des Messias, dann komm und iss mit uns.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell; preserves explicit 1sg-to-1pl reformulation with constant patient. Covers both tokens 4 and 5 once.

data.turoyo: maʕmaḏḏe u zʕuro b əšme d Mšiḥo w ršəmme bayne ʕayne w yatu axile aʕmayye.
data.translation: sie tauften den Jungen im Namen des Messias und machten das (Kreuz)zeichen auf seiner Stirn. Dann setzte er sich hin und aß mit ihnen.

rationale: Thin III Preterit cell; plural agents and overt zero-marked boy patient.

data.turoyo: komər azzi aʕmayye, maʕməḏalli b əšme d Mšiḥo w aṯino mən awi?
data.translation: Ich ging mit ihnen, sie tauften mich im Namen des Messias, und jetzt bin ich gekommen – was ist schon passiert?

rationale: Thin III Preterit cell; plural baptizers with 1sg suffix patient, contrasts with overt nominal patient.

data.turoyo: Maṣlawle lu qašo ʕar riša w mʕamḏole. Mhəlle a tləṯ aʕle.
data.translation: Der Pfaffe liess sie nun beichten und taufte sie, dann traute er ihm die drei Frauen an.

rationale: Thin III Preterit cell; feminine patient indexed in mʕamḏole. With two inherited examples the cell now reaches five.

data.turoyo: Mu sababano Šamʕən Faṭruṣ mqadašle maye du tuʕmiḏo w ġəṭle bayn am maye mqadše parrat d ilono yaroqo.
data.translation: Daher weihte Simon Petrus tauf Wasser und tauchte in das geweihte Wasser zweige eines grünes Baumes

rationale: Thin inherited III Detransitive Infinitiv cell; tuʕmiḏo as a baptism event nominal in maye du tuʕmiḏo, not a finite patient-subject form.

summary: I ʕəmḏo has the baptized participant as subject; III active has a baptizer and a patient (zero nominal or suffix), while overt III Detransitive mtaʕmiḏi places recipients as subject. English or German semantic voice does not determine morphology (94/48).
JTM 4.2 consistently uses b əšme d Mšiḥo as the naming formula. In 94/48 b- marks water and chrism instead. These transparent ritual frames do not require a separate idiom or sense.

Inherited tuʕmiḏo is retained in III Detransitive Infinitiv by the entry's convention. Its nominal task/genitive contexts do not require a passive interpretation. ʕamaḏe and ʕmoḏo are held outside firm new verbal boxes pending morphological verification.
The active person title Maʕməḏono belongs with Part act.; the inherited spelling Maʕmiḏono and its references are preserved by moving the existing example rather than rewriting it.

MAC NE interview 1/11: is dmaʕmaḏ reduced Detransitive, an active-shaped receptive form, or a different construction? Does gmaʕmḏina mean customary Epiphany self-washing, receiving baptism, or baptizing others?
JTM 4.4/20: is ʕamaḏe a plural noun 'baptisms'? Should ʕmoḏo at 12/23 and 94/48 be a lexical noun or the I Infinitiv? No new box is published from these ambiguous records.
12/8: verify missing alfo after tloṯ against the edition; the supplied German says three thousand while the supplied Turoyo says three.
Talay 1/102: confirm maʕmaḏna segmentation and provide a matching edition translation for this token; the supplied German omits its apparent baptism clause.
At Epiphany gmaʕmḏina is juxtaposed with washing and putting cold water on one's own head. A commemorative ritual application is suggested; exact participant structure remains unresolved.
